structuralDecisions.decision: Replace the L.tileLayer(OSM) call in LocationsView.vue's onMounted with a single L.imageOverlay() call over an in-repo image, keeping Leaflet's default EPSG:3857 CRS on the existing L.map('map') instance. No new component, class, or package is introduced.
structuralDecisions.rationale: This is a one-line substitution of a tile source inside an already-established pattern (a single Vue view owning its own Leaflet map instance). CLAUDE.md's architect-skip criterion — 'purely additive within an established pattern' — applies directly: no new base class, no layer-boundary change, no cross-cutting concern. The analyst's own architecturalFlags entry already reached this conclusion; this review confirms it against the actual file rather than taking it on faith.
tradeOffs: A static image overlay cannot pan/zoom-stream new detail the way real tiles can, but the feature's own purpose (deterministic, network-free test fixture) makes that a non-issue, not a cost.

The image's lat/lng bounds box must be hand-sized to cover all three shop coordinates, the Sword Coast polygon, and the zoom-6 flyTo target — a magic-number risk that lands on the developer, not on structure.

structuralDecisions.decision: Keep the new map image and its licence note physically beside each other under apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/public/ (e.g. sword-coast-map.png + sword-coast-map.LICENSE.txt), matching the existing flat-file convention already used there (aurelis.jpg, logo.png, favicon.svg).
structuralDecisions.rationale: apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/public/ is Vite's static-asset root; files here are served byte-for-byte from the app's own origin with no build-time processing, which is exactly the same-origin guarantee acceptance criterion #1 depends on. No new directory or asset pipeline is justified for one image.
tradeOffs: Flat public/ placement works at the current scale (four static assets); it would need revisiting only if this app accumulates many map/image assets, which is not this feature's concern.

fitness.property: The map image is served from the app's own origin with zero cross-origin requests during /locations load
fitness.verification: Playwright: new test in tests/map.spec.ts that page.route()-aborts any request whose URL is not same-origin, asserting the route handler never fires for a non-origin request and leaflet.checkTileFailures() is false

structuralDecisions.decision: Do not introduce L.CRS.Simple or any non-default CRS; L.map('map') keeps its current no-crs-argument call, so Leaflet's default EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator) continues to back every coordinate in the view.
structuralDecisions.rationale: map.spec.ts's assertions (map centre ≈ [45.0, -120.0], zoom-10 bounds, geolocation flyTo to [47.6, -121.1], Turf.js distance 300–400km between Waterdeep and Baldur's Gate) are all computed against real-world lat/lng under EPSG:3857. Switching to L.CRS.Simple — the usual pairing for a static image overlay — would silently invalidate every one of those assertions by changing what a 'degree' means on the map. This is the one decision in this feature where getting it wrong breaks the pipeline's own stated acceptance criteria, which is why it's called out explicitly rather than left as an implementation detail.
tradeOffs: The image's bounds box has to be sized in real lat/lng degrees (a trapezoid-shaped projection distortion at this latitude) rather than simple pixel-to-unit image coordinates, which is slightly less intuitive to size by hand than L.CRS.Simple would be.

fitness.property: map.spec.ts's real-geography assertions (centre, zoom-10 bounds, geolocation pan, Turf distance) keep passing unchanged
fitness.verification: tests/map.spec.ts run via scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh in CI; any CRS regression fails these tests directly, no separate lint rule needed since the existing test suite already encodes this invariant

componentPlacement.component: Sword Coast map image overlay (L.imageOverlay call + its source image)
componentPlacement.reason: LocationsView.vue already owns its Leaflet map instance end-to-end (markers, polygon, popups, layer control); the tile-to-image swap is a change inside that existing ownership boundary, not a new one. public/ is the app's existing static-asset root.

crossings: packages/saturday-playwright-leaflet's test fixture contract (waitForMapLoad/checkTileFailures) — relied on read-only, not modified by this feature
tests/reagent-map-globe.spec.ts's off-origin-request-blocking pattern — reused, not owned, by the new no-network test

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: LocationsView.vue (adapter/UI layer) may depend on Leaflet (framework) directly — no domain or use-case layer exists in this app for map rendering to violate
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: This app has no Clean-Architecture domain/use-case split around the map feature; LocationsView.vue is itself the framework-facing component. loom MCP graph tools were not used — the repo graph/index availability wasn't verified, and the change is small enough that a direct read of the single file (apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/src/views/LocationsView.vue) was sufficient to confirm this, stated here per the fallback-disclosure requirement.

antiPatternChecks.notes: A single L.imageOverlay() call was chosen over introducing an asset-loading abstraction or configurable tile-source strategy; nothing in this feature's scope needs more than one static image, so no abstraction is justified.
No new abstraction is introduced, so there is nothing to leak.
